# Lighthouse

Lighthouse is the project's decision memory. A **decision** is what was
decided and why; **rules** are the checks the engine compiles from decisions;
every change is checked against them. A **judgment** (`pass`, `fail` or
`notApplicable`) is a label on one finding; a **suppression** says a finding
that is right is left in place on purpose, either in the code (a directive) or
outside it (`external`, recorded with a justification). A finding someone
judged is remembered with its reason and is not raised again.

## The loop

1. **Check** the files you changed: MCP tool `check` (with `changed: true`), or
   `lighthouse check --changed --format json`.
2. **Understand** the findings: they come grouped by decision, then by file.
   A group says once what its decision requires and what the code should look
   like (`expected`), plus the evidence all its findings share; a finding is
   `[line:col, message, fingerprint prefix]` with the evidence that sets it
   apart as an optional fourth element. For more (the context, every example),
   read the decision: MCP resource `lighthouse://decisions/<id>`, tool
   `decision_show`, or `lighthouse decision show <id>`. `detail: "full"` (`--detail full`)
   returns one self-contained record per finding instead.
3. **Fix** the code, then **recheck**. Each group says how its decision is
   fixed: `fix` names who makes the fix, its `safety` (`safe` or `unsafe`),
   whether it runs here and the call that applies it, and `brief` marks a
   decision whose findings you fix by hand with the brief of `review_show`.
   The loop:
   1. `check`.
   2. `fix` the groups whose `fix` is `safe` and runs.
   3. For the others, `review_show` the finding, edit with its brief, `check` again.
   4. An `unsafe` fix that runs (every fix by a model is) is previewed first: `fix` the group, read the diffs, then run the `apply` of a preview to write exactly that fix. Passing `noModels` asks no model.
   A check shows no diff; `fix` does. Only `safe` fixes are written, whoever
   makes them; an `unsafe` fix is shown as a preview with its diff, unless the project's `[fix] unsafe = true`
   or `unsafeFixes` says otherwise. Every fix is verified and rolled back if it
   makes the file worse. Review the diff like any other change. A run that
   reports `incomplete` did not check everything: it is not a pass.
4. **Judge** the findings that ask for review (`review_list`: those of
   decisions that authored `warn` or `info`, whatever level the configuration
   reports them at): fix them, or record a judgment with `review_resolve`.
   `fail` means the finding is right; add `suppress: {justification}` to leave
   it in place on purpose. `pass` means the code conforms (a false positive).
   `notApplicable` means the decision does not apply here, a hint to narrow
   it. Give a `reason` that says why, written for the next reader. Pass `seen`
   (the `seen` evidence of a review task) so a judgment is refused if the
   finding changed under you. A fingerprint prefix as shown names the finding;
   an ambiguous or shorter than 7 characters one is refused. `review_show`
   reads one finding in full.

## Rules of conduct

- Never suppress an error to make it go away. Fix the code.
  The only exception is an inline directive
  `lighthouse-disable-next-line <rule> -- <reason>` (or `-line`, or a
  `lighthouse-disable` ... `lighthouse-enable` range) with a real reason; it
  is reviewed in the diff.
- A judgment never hides an error; if the rule is wrong, narrow it with
  `decision_update` (it is tested before it is written).
- When the same decision comes up twice, write it down: `decision_create` writes
  a project-local decision under `.lighthouse/decisions` and rejects it unless
  its examples pass.
- Analysis always covers the whole project; paths and `changed` only narrow
  what is reported.

## Looking things up

Do not memorize decision text; ask for it when a finding names a rule.

- `decision_list` lists decisions; `lighthouse://catalog` is the index.
- `lighthouse://decisions/<id>` renders one decision (context, requirement,
  examples).
- `lighthouse://config` is the effective configuration.
- `review_history` shows every judgment recorded on a finding.

## Active decisions (6)

A decision declares the severity of its findings: `error` is definitive, so it needs no review and only a directive in the code suppresses it; `warn` and `info` are review tasks, and a judgment can hide them whatever level the configuration reports them at. `fixable: safe|unsafe` marks a decision with a fixer and the safety of its fix.

### core

- `core/max-lines` (warn) Files stay small and cohesive
- `core/max-len` (warn) Lines fit the configured width
- `core/allow-reason` (error) Allow a finding in source, with a reason
- `core/no-unused-allow` (warn, fixable: unsafe) Allow annotations suppress something
- `core/decision-naming` (warn) Decision names follow the ESLint convention
- `core/formatted` (error, fixable: safe) Source files use their standard formatter
